name: skills
description: In-house Claude Code skills, plus vetted third-party plugins pinned to reviewed commits

plugins.name: humanizer
plugins.description: Rewrite AI-sounding text so it reads like the writer without changing what it says. Third-party, MIT, pinned to a reviewed commit.

plugins.name: context-mode
plugins.description: Routes large tool output through a local sandbox and an FTS5 index instead of the context window. Third-party, Elastic License 2.0 (source-available, NOT open source), pinned to a reviewed commit. Its hooks intercept Bash, Read, Grep, WebFetch and Agent calls, and ctx_execute runs arbitrary code by design.

plugins.name: session-memory
plugins.description: Cross-session memory: compresses session transcripts into a searchable store. Third-party, Apache-2.0, pinned to a reviewed commit. Runs a persistent local worker, auto-installs Bun, uv and Chroma, hooks every tool call, and sends transcripts to an LLM provider for compression. PostHog telemetry ships on by default: run `npx claude-mem telemetry disable` after installing. Do not use it in a session handling client material under NDA without checking where compression runs.

plugins.name: next-steps
plugins.description: After each turn, suggests up to three next prompts above the input. Press 1, 2 or 3 to put one in the prompt box as a draft you can edit, 0 to dismiss. Third-party, MIT, pinned to a reviewed commit. A function-hooks plugin with no skills: after every answer of 80 characters or more it forks the session for one short extra model call, and it never submits a prompt on its own.

plugins.name: token-weather-usage
plugins.description: One band above the prompt: context tokens with a weather icon, the 5-hour and 7-day limits against the time elapsed, the prompt cache's time left, the session cost and the running subagents. This copy of Eric Cologni's plugin (Apache-2.0, upstream 701aa6f): in the desktop app the pills wrap to fit the band. No network requests and no model calls.

plugins.name: flightdeck
plugins.description: A live pane of the session's permission checks and subagents, one lane per agent. This copy of Stephen Casella's plugin (MIT, upstream f31daca): by default it shows only the permission gate and the agents, every agent gets a lane, and options bring back the header, time axis and card details. No file, process, network or model access.
